Sarı Yüz, ilk sayfadan son sayfaya temposunu hiç düşürmeden, çeşitlilik, ırkçılık ve kültürel sömürü gibi önemli meseleleri işlerken sosyal medyanın ürkütücü yüzünü de etkileyici bir şekilde ortaya koyuyor.

name: Kurt Kanunu
label: simple
description: Kurt Kanunu, ilk olarak Ulus gazetesinde tefrika edilir (1967-1968). Kitap neşri ise daha sonra 1969’da Bilgi Yayınevince gerçekleştirilir. Kurt Kanunu, Kemal Tahir’in yakın dönem Türkiye tarihini bir nehir roman dizisi şeklinde ele alma teşebbüsünün beşinci kitabı olarak değerlendirilebilir. Kemal Tahir, Kurt Kanunu’yla Kurtuluş Savaşı sonrasında yeniden tanımlanan siyasetin biçimlenme dinamikleriyle ekonomik ve politik temellerini, Takrir-i Sükun Kanunu’ndan sonra Türkiye’nin siyasi ve düşünsel iklimini, birlikte siyaset yapan kadroların "İzmir Suikastı" etrafında kendi içlerinde yaşadığı tasfiyeye varan gerilimlerle çatışmaları ve eski savaşçılarla siyasetçilerin dramını bireysel ve toplumsal boyutlarıyla romanlaştırır. Kurt Kanunu, dönemin gerçek aktörlerini birer roman karakterine dönüştürerek bu aktörlerin hem 1908’den hem de 1923’ten sonraki siyaset biçim ve pratiklerini çok boyutlu bir sorgulamaya tabi tutar. Serüven romanı tadındaki eser; hızlı akan yapısı, hareketli ve zengin olay örgüsüyle karakterlerin bireysel ve toplumsal dramlarını bü - yüleyici ve gerçekçi bir dille işler. Kurt Kanunu, Kemal Tahir külliyatının başyapıtları arasında yer alır.

name: Yere düşen yapraklar
label: simple
tags: Yere düşen yapraklar; yere dusen yapraklar; yapraklar
description: Seneler önceydi... Bir taşın arkasına saklanmıştım. Evet, tam on iki yaşındaydım. O günü hiç unutmadım. Bilmem ki şu çektiklerim o günün kefareti mi? Sadece saklanmıştım, bir de bakakalmıştım: Bir baba, bir küçük kız ve bir de kazılmış çukura... Hem neye bakıyordum ki? Küçük bir kızın gömülmesine mi, yoksa toprağa çoktan gömdüğüm vicdanıma mı? Kapattım kulaklarımı semaya yükselen kızın çığlıklarına... Ah duymaz olaydım! Önce "Babaaa..." diye bir çığlık attı. Zaten onu gömen babası değil miydi? Sonra "Anneee..." diye bir çığlık. Etrafta kimseler yoktu, onu duyan da. Ve sonra "Kardeşiiim..." diye bir ses gelmez mi? Bana mı seslenmişti? Hayır! Hayır! Baba, süratle toprağı kızın üzerine savurdu. Ne yapacağımı bilemedim... Zaten başıma ne geldiyse hep bilmediğimden gelmemiş miydi? Hayatımda kimi zaman sevgiye bürünen harfler bir bir kılıçtan geçirildi. Oluk oluk kan aktı eliften, mimden ve nundan... Kelimeler anlamını yitirdi. Revan olmuş gönlüme hicranlı bekleyişler kaldı. Anlamsız cümleler ve boş serzenişler...

name: Ana
label: simple
description: Ünlü Rus yazarı Aleksey Maksimoviç Peşkov ya da herkesin bildiği adıyla Maksim Gorki, 1868’de Novgorod’da doğdu. Küçük yaşta yetim kaldı, okuyamadı. Uzun süre başıboş, yoksul bir hayat sürdü. ’Acı’ anlamına gelen Gorki takma adını alması bu yüzdendir. Yazarlığa romantik öykülerle başladı; öykülerinde gururlu, özgürlüğü seçmiş kahramanların başkaldırışları anlatılır. İlk romanı Foma (1899) ve özellikle Ayak Takımı Arasında (1902) adlı oyunu ona dünya çapında ün sağladı. Daha sonra Çar yönetimiyle uyuşmazlığa düştüğü için hapsedildi; hapisten çıkınca en büyük devrimci yapıtı olan Ana’yı yazdı. 1917’deki Büyük Rus Devrimi’nden sonra, sağlık sorunları nedeniyle bir süre İtalya’ya gönderildi. Kendi hayatını anlatan kitaplar yazdı: Çocukluğum (1913-14), Ekmeğimi Kazanırken (1915-16), Benim Üniversitelerim (1923). 1936 yılında dünyaca ünlü bir yazar olarak Moskova’da ölen Maksim Gorki’nin adı, doğduğu kente verildi.

name: Shaxsiy rivojlanishning 33 qoidasi
label: simple
description: "Shaxsiy rivojlanishning 33 qoidasi" ongli yashash va barqaror kamolotga yetaklovchi ilhombaxsh qo‘llanma. Asar shaxsiy rivojni bir martalik natija emas, balki uzluksiz ichki mehnat ekanini ko‘rsatadi.  Kitob ichki poklikni asrash, "ichimizdagi bola"ni yo‘qotmaslik va hayot sinovlarini donolik hamda ruhiy kuch manbaiga aylantirish g‘oyasini ilgari suradi. Har bir lahza o‘sish uchun berilgan imkoniyat sifatida talqin etiladi.  Asar minnatdorlik, insoniylik va oddiy hayot go‘zalliklarini his qilishni mustahkamlab, o‘quvchini nafaqat muvaffaqiyatli, balki ma’nan boy va baxtli inson bo‘lishga chorlaydi.

label: simple
genres: Badiiy adabiyotlar; Jahon adabiyoti; Siyosiy adabiyotlar
description: "1984" Jorj Oruell qalamiga mansub siyosiy antiutopik roman bo‘lib, totalitar tuzum ostidagi jamiyatning dahshatli manzarasini tasvirlaydi. Asar syujeti Okeaniya davlati poytaxti Londonda yashovchi Partiya a’zosi Uinston Smit atrofida kechadi. Katta og‘a boshchiligidagi hukmron Partiya odamlarning har bir qadamini kuzatadi, tarixni qayta yozadi, "Yangitil" orqali erkin fikrlashni yo‘q qilishga intiladi. Uinston ich-ichidan bu tizimga qarshi bo‘lsa-da, qo‘rquv va shubha talvasasida yashaydi. U Juliya bilan bo‘lgan muhabbati orqali ozodlikka intiladi, ammo yakunda Partiyaning shafqatsiz ta’qibiga uchrab, ruhiy va jismoniy jihatdan sindiriladi. Roman o‘quvchini "haqiqat" va "erkinlik" tushunchalarini qayta ko‘rib chiqishga undaydi va totalitarizmning inson ruhiga yetkazadigan zararini his etishga yordam beradi.

name: Hard-boiled Wonderland and the End of the World
label: simple
tags: Hard-boiled Wonderland and the end of the World
description: In this hyperkinetic and relentlessly inventive novel, Japan’s most popular (and controversial) fiction writer hurtles into the consciousness of the West. Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World draws readers into a narrative particle accelerator in which a split-brained data processor, a deranged scientist, his shockingly undemure granddaughter, Lauren Bacall, Bob Dylan, and various thugs, librarians, and subterranean monsters collide to dazzling effect. What emerges is simultaneously cooler than zero and unaffectedly affecting, a hilariously funny and deeply serious meditation on the nature and uses of the mind.

name: Tales from the cafe
label: simple
description: In a back alley in Tokyo, there is a café that has been serving carefully brewed coffee for more than one hundred years. Local legend says that this shop offers something else besides coffee-the chance to travel back in time. With faces both familiar and new, Tales from the Cafe follows the story of four patrons who visit to take advantage of café Funiculi Funicula’s time-traveling offer and revisit moments with family, friends and lovers. Each one must face up to the past to move on with their lives. Kawaguchi’s wistful and heartwarming new novel once again invites the reader to ask themselves, "What would you do if you could travel back in time?"

name: Before your memory fades
label: simple
description: In Before Your Memory Fades, we meet: the daughter who resents her deceased parents for leaving her orphaned; the comedian who aches for his beloved and their shared dreams; the sister whose grief has become all-consuming; and the man who realized his love for his childhood friend.  Heart-warming and poignant, Kawaguchi explores how holding on to the past can affect our future, and asks the reader: would you travel in time if your actions couldn't change the present?

name: Before we say goodbye
label: simple
description: 'Soon I will pour you a cup of coffee, Kazu explained while placing the cup in front of Michiko.  Coffee?' Michiko cocked her head inquisitively. She didn't see the connection between going back in time and coffee.  'The time you may spend back in the past is limited, from the time I pour the coffee until the time the coffee gets cold.'

name: There are rivers in the sky
label: simple
tags: There are rivers in the sky
description: This is the story of one lost poem, two great rivers and three remarkable lives - all connected by a single drop of water. In the ruins of Nineveh, an ancient city of Mesopotamia, there lies, hidden in the sand, fragments of a long-forgotten poem, the Epic of Gilgamesh. In Victorian London, an extraordinary child is born at the edge of the dirt-black River Thames. Arthur’s only chance of escaping poverty is his brilliant memory. When his gift earns him a spot as an apprentice at a printing press, Arthur’s world opens up far beyond the slums, with one book sending him across the seas: Nineveh and Its Remains. In Turkey in 2014, Narin, a Yazidi girl living by the River Tigris, waits to be baptized with water brought from the holy Lalish in Iraq. The ceremony is cruelly interrupted, and soon Narin and her grandmother must journey across war-torn lands in the hope of reaching the sacred valley of their people.  In London in 2018, broken-hearted Zaleekhah, a hydrologist, moves to a houseboat on the Thames to escape the wreckage of her marriage. Zaleekhah foresees a life drained of all love and meaning, until an unexpected connection to her homeland changes everything.  A dazzling feat of storytelling from one of the greatest writers of our time, Elif Shafak's There are Rivers in the Sky is a rich, sweeping novel that spans centuries, continents and cultures, entwined by rivers, rains and waterdrops: 'Water remembers.  It is humans who forget.'

name: And the Mountains Echoed
label: simple
description: Afghanistan, 1952. Abdullah and his sister Pari live with their father and stepmother in the small village of Shadbagh. Their father, Saboor, is constantly in search of work and they struggle together through poverty and brutal winters. To Abdullah, Pari - as beautiful and sweet-natured as the fairy for which she was named - is everything. More like a parent than a brother, Abdullah will do anything for her, even trading his only pair of shoes for a feather for her treasured collection. Each night they sleep together in their cot, their heads touching, their limbs tangled.  One day the siblings journey across the desert to Kabul with their father. Pari and Abdullah have no sense of the fate that awaits them there, for the event which unfolds will tear their lives apart; sometimes a finger must be cut to save the hand. Crossing generations and continents, moving from Kabul, to Paris, to San Francisco, to the Greek island of Tinos, Khaled Hosseini writes about the bonds that define us and shape our lives. With profound wisdom, depth, insight and compassion he explores the ways in which we help our loved ones in need, how the choices we make resonate through history and how we are often surprised by the people closest to us.

name: The next person you meet in heaven
label: simple
tags: The next person you meet in heaven

name: Things we never got over
label: simple
description: Bearded, bad-boy barber Knox prefers to live his life the way he takes his coffee: alone. Unless you count his basset hound, Waylon. Knox doesn’t tolerate drama, even when it comes in the form of a stranded runaway bride. Naomi wasn’t just running away from her wedding. She was riding to the rescue of her estranged twin to Knockemout, Virginia, a rough-around-the-edges town where disputes are settled the old-fashioned way... with fists and beer. Usually in that order. Too bad for Naomi her evil twin hasn’t changed at all. After helping herself to Naomi’s car and cash, Tina leaves her with something unexpected. The niece Naomi didn’t know she had. Now she’s stuck in town with no car, no job, no plan, and no home with an eleven-year-old going on thirty to take care of.

name: November 9
label: simple
description: Fallon meets Ben, an aspiring novelist, the day of her scheduled cross-country move. Their untimely attraction leads them to spend Fallon’s last day in L.A. together, and her eventful life becomes the creative inspiration Ben has always sought for his novel. Over time and amidst the various relationships and tribulations of their own separate lives, they continue to meet on the same date every year. Until one day Fallon becomes unsure if Ben has been telling her the truth or fabricating a perfect reality for the sake of the ultimate plot twist.  Can Ben’s relationship with Fallon - and simultaneously his novel be considered a love story if it ends in heartbreak?

name: Brave New World
label: simple
description: Far in the future, the World Controllers have created the ideal society. Through clever use of genetic engineering, brainwashing and recreational sex and drugs all its members are happy consumers. Bernard Marx seems alone harbouring an ill-defined longing to break free. A visit to one of the few remaining Savage Reservations where the old, imperfect life still continues, may be the cure for his distress...  Huxley's ingenious fantasy of the future sheds a blazing light on the present and is considered to be his most enduring masterpiece.

name: Conversations with Friends
label: simple
description: Frances is twenty-one years old, cool-headed and observant. A student in Dublin and an aspiring writer, at night she performs spoken word with her best friend Bobbi, who used to be her girlfriend. When they are interviewed and then befriended by Melissa, a well-known journalist, who is married to Nick, an actor, they enter into a world of beautiful houses, raucous dinner parties and holidays in Brittany. But when Frances and Nick get unexpectedly closer, the sharply witty and emotion-averse Frances is forced to honestly confront her own vulnerabilities for the first time.

name: Fight Club
label: simple
description: Chuck Palahniuk showed himself to be his generation’s most visionary satirist in this, his first book. Fight Club’s estranged narrator leaves his lackluster job when he comes under the thrall of Tyler Durden, an enigmatic young man who holds secret after-hours boxing matches in the basements of bars. There, two men fight "as long as they have to." This is a gloriously original work that exposes the darkness at the core of our modern world. And remember: "The first rule about fight club is you don’t talk about fight club."

name: The sun and her flowers (english - russian)
label: simple
description: Долгожданная вторая книга Рупи Каур, автора бестселлера “Milk and Ноnеу”, переведенного на 39 языков и проданного тиражом 3 миллиона экземпляров.  “The Sun and Her Flowers” сборник белых стихов о росте и исцелении, происхождении и уважении к своим корням, эмиграции и умении найти дом внутри себя. Это рецепт жизни и праздник любви во всех ее проявлениях, книга, уже покорившая сердца миллионов читателей по всему миру.  Переводы стихов публикуются с оригинальными текстами на английском языке и уникальными авторскими иллюстрациями.

name: In Five Years
label: simple
description: Dannie Kohan lives her life by the numbers. She is nothing like her lifelong best friend - the wild, whimsical, believes-in-fate Bella. Dannie’s meticulous planning seems to have paid off after she nails the most important job interview of her career and accepts her boyfriend’s marriage proposal in one fell swoop, falling asleep completely content. But when she awakens, she’s suddenly in a different apartment, with a different ring on her finger, and beside a very different man. Dannie spends exactly one hour five years in the future before she wakes again in her own home on the brink of midnight and it is one hour she cannot shake. In Five Years is an unforgettable love story, but it is not the one you’re expecting.

name: King of Pride
label: simple
description: Reserved, controlled, and proper to a fault, Kai Young has neither the time nor inclination for chaos - and Isabella, with her purple hair and inappropriate jokes, is chaos personified. With a crucial CEO vote looming and a media empire at stake, the billionaire heir can’t afford the distraction she brings. Isabella is everything he shouldn’t want, but with every look and every touch, he’s tempted to break all his rules...and claim her as his own. Bold, impulsive, and full of life, Isabella Valencia has never met a party she doesn’t like or a man she couldn’t charm... except for Kai Young. It shouldn’t matter. He’s not her type - the man translates classics into Latin for fun, and his membership at the exclusive club where she bartends means he’s strictly off - limits. But she can’t deny that, beneath his cool exterior, is a man who could make her melt with just a touch. No matter how hard they try, they can’t resist giving in to their forbidden desires. Even if it costs them everything.

name: Beach read
label: simple
description: Augustus Everett is an acclaimed author of literary fiction. January Andrews writes bestselling romance. When she pens a Happily Ever After, he kills off his entire cast. They’re polar opposites. In fact, the only thing they have in common is that for the next three months they’re living in neighboring beach houses, broke and bogged down with writer’s block. Then one hazy evening, one thing leads to another and they strike a deal designed to force them out of their creative ruts: Augustus will spend the summer writing something happy, and January will pen the next Great American Novel. She’ll take him on field trips worthy of any rom-com montage, and he’ll take her to interview surviving members of a backwoods death cult (obviously). Everyone will finish a book and no one will fall in love. Really.

name: Too Late
label: simple
description: Sloan will go through hell and back for those she loves. And she does, every single day. After finding herself stuck in a relationship with the dangerous and morally corrupt Asa Jackson, Sloan will do whatever it takes to get by until she’s able to find a way out. Nothing will get in her way. Nothing except Carter. Sloan is the best thing to ever happen to Asa. And if you ask Asa, he’d say he’s the best thing to ever happen to Sloan. Despite Slaan’s disapproval of Asa’s sinister lifestyle, he does exactly what he needs to do in order to stay a step ahead in his business. He also does exactly what he needs to do in order to stay a step ahead of Sloan.. Nothing will get in his way. Nothing except Carter.

name: Speak
label: simple
description: "Speak up for yourself-we want to know what you have to say." From the first moment of her freshman year at Merryweather High, Melinda knows this is a big fat lie, part of the nonsense of high school. She is friendless, outcast, because she busted an end-of-summer party by calling the cops, so now nobody will talk to her, let alone listen to her. As time passes, she becomes increasingly isolated and practically stops talking altogether. Only her art class offers any solace, and it is through her work on an art project that she is finally able to face what really happened at that terrible party. Her healing process has just begun when she has another violent encounter. But this time Melinda cannot stay silent. A timeless novel about consent and finding the courage to speak up for yourself, this twentieth anniversary edition includes all - new bonus content: an introduction by Ashley C. Ford, an original poem and essay by Laurie Halse Anderson as well as a question-and-answer dialogue with her, an afterword by Jason Reynolds, and an updated resource list for survivors of sexual violence.

name: The lessons of history
label: simple
description: A concise survey of the culture and civilization of mankind, The Lessons of History is the result of a lifetime of research from Pulitzer Prize - winning historians Will and Ariel Durant. With their accessible compendium of philosophy and social progress, the Durants take us on a journey through history, exploring the possibilities and limitations of humanity over time. Juxtaposing the great lives, ideas, and accomplishments with cycles of war and conquest, the Durants reveal the towering themes of history and give meaning to our own.

name: Curtain
label: simple
description: Captain Hastings' invitation to a reunion with his old friend Hercule Poirot brings them full circle, back to the rambling country house of Styles where they solved their first murder together.  But both Poirot and Styles have seen better days. Despite being crippled with arthritis, there seems to be nothing wrong with the great detective's ‘little grey cells' - until he brands one of the seemingly harmless guests a five- times murderer. Have Hercule Poirot's deductive instincts finally deserted him, or is there really a serial killer determined to bring down the curtain on all of them?

name: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
label: simple
description: After the Great War, life can never be the same again. Wounds need healing, and the horror of violent death banished into memory.  Captain Arthur Hastings is invited to the rolling country estate of Styles to recuperate from injuries sustained at the Front. It is the last place he expects to encounter murder. Fortunately he knows a former detective, a Belgian refugee, who has grown bored of retirement...

name: The Suspect
label: simple
description: When the UK’s favourite breakfast TV presenter dies live on air in front of millions of viewers, the nation is left devastated. Even more so when it becomes clear that her death was not an accident. All of the evidence points to celebrity chef Sebastian Brooks. But junior barrister Adam Green is about to discover that the case is not as open-and-shut as it seems. And although the presenter’s angelic persona would suggest otherwise, she was not short of enemies in the glittery TV world ... Can Adam uncover the truth?

name: The Maidens
label: simple
description: E dward Fosca is a murderer. Of this Mariana is certain. But Fosca is untouchable. A handsome and charismatic Greek tragedy professor at Cambridge University, Fosca is adored by staff and students alike - particularly by the members of a secret society of female students known as the Maidens. Mariana Andros is a brilliant but troubled group therapist who becomes fixated on the Maidens when one member, a friend of Mariana’s niece Zoe, is found murdered in Cambridge. Mariana, who was once herself a student at the university, quickly suspects that behind the idyllic beauty of the spires and turrets, and beneath the ancient traditions, lies something sinister. And she becomes convinced that, despite his alibi, Edward Fosca is guilty of the murder. But why would the professor target one of his students? And why does he keep returning to the rites of Persephone, the maiden, and her journey to the underworld? When another body is found, Mariana’s obsession with proving Fosca’s guilt spirals out of control, threatening to destroy her credibility as well as her closest relationships. But Mariana is determined to stop this killer, even if it costs her everything - including her own life.

name: Hell Bent
label: simple
description: Wealth. Power. Murder. Magic. Alex Stern is back and the Ivy League is going straight to hell.  Find a gateway to the underworld. Steal a soul out of hell. A simple plan, except people who make this particular journey rarely come back. But Galaxy 'Alex' Stern is determined to break Darlington out of purgatory - even if it costs her a future at Lethe and at Yale.  Forbidden from attempting a rescue, Alex and Dawes can't call on the Ninth House for help, so they assemble a team of dubious allies to save the gentleman of Lethe. Together, they will have to navigate a maze of arcane texts and bizarre artifacts to uncover the societies' most closely guarded secrets, and break every rule doing it. But when faculty members begin to die off, Alex knows these aren't just accidents. Something deadly is at work in New Haven, and if she is going to survive, she'll have to reckon with the monsters of her past and a darkness built into the university's very walls.  Thick with history and packed with Bardugo's signature twists, Hell Bent brings to life an intricate world full of magic, violence, and all too real monsters.

name: A portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
label: simple
tags: A portrait of the artist as a young man; moysklad:e1295e64-d132-11ec-0a80-0e2100b5001d
description: "A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man" by James Joyce is a novel that delves into the inner world of its protagonist, Stephen Dedalus, as he navigates the complexities of religion, nationality, and artistic expression in early 20th-century Ireland. Throughout the novel, Joyce employs stream-of-consciousness narrative techniques, intricate symbolism, and rich language to explore Stephen’s inner turmoil and quest for self-realization. The title itself suggests the novel’s focus on the development of an artist’s identity amid the constraints of society and tradition.

name: The Bazaar of Bad Dreams
label: simple
description: There is a treasure here for every reader:  a man who keeps reliving exactly the same life, repeating his mistakes over and over again; a columnist who kills people by writing their obituaries; a poignant tale about the end of the human race and a firework competition between neighbours which reaches an explosive climax.

name: Broken Throne
label: simple
genres: Badiiy adabiyotlar; Fantastika; Zamonaviy jahon adabiyoti
description: Delve into the dark and dangerous world of Red Queen with this must-have companion, which includes three brand-new short stories as well as extra scenes, maps, family trees, flags, and much more. This masterful collection offers an entirely new look into the beloved characters in the iconic Red Queen series, where no one is as they appear, and the only certainty is betrayal.

name: The Atlas Six
label: simple
genres: Badiiy adabiyotlar; Fantastika; Zamonaviy jahon adabiyoti
description: Once a decade, the world's best magicians are invited to join the elite Alexandrian Society. Its members enjoy a lifetime of power and access to ancient secrets. But only five places are offered. So, after recruitment by the mysterious Atlas Blakely, the candidates must complete a rigorous year of arcane study.  Libby Rhodes and Nico de Varona are inseparable enemies and cosmologists who can control matter with their minds. Parisa Kamali is a telepath, Reina Mori understands the flow of life itself and Callum Nova can manipulate desires. Finally, there's Tristan Caine, whose powers mystify even himself. The rivals must survive their trials. And if they can prove themselves, they will. Most of them.

name: What I talk about when I talk about running
label: simple
tags: What I talk about when I talk about running
description: In 1982, having sold his jazz bar to devote himself to writing, Murakami began running to keep fit. A year later, he’d completed a solo course from Athens to Marathon, and now, after dozens of such races, he reflects upon the influence the sport has had on his life and on his writing. Equal parts travelogue, training log, and reminiscence, this revealing memoir covers his four-month preparation for the 2005 New York City Marathon and settings ranging from Tokyo‘s Jingu Gaien gardens, where he once shared the course with an Olympian, to the Charles River in Boston. This is a must-read for fans of this masterful yet private writer as well as for the exploding population of athletes who find similar satisfaction in distance running.

name: Wuthering Heights
label: simple
description: Years ago, feeling sorry for a nameless orphan, the master of Wuthering Heights decided to take the boy into his home and raise him alongside his own children. The foster child grew into a proud and cruel young man, passionately in love with the master’s daughter. Their mutual feelings promised happiness. So why now, years later, does the wind knock on the windows of her childhood room at night, pleading in a woman’s voice to be let in?  Wuthering Heightsby Emily Brontë is a classic of Gothic literature. It is a sophisticated exploration of love and villainy, a novel about ferocious passion that borders on cruelty, and how the sins of parents echo in the lives of their descendants.

name: A Room of One's Own
label: simple
description: Virginia Woolf (1882-1941) was an English writer, publisher and literary critic, considered to be one of the major modernist figures in the United Kingdom and beyond. Her intricate, non-linear prose style is widely known as the stream of consciousness and her numerous essays became a perfect specimen of genre. A Room of One's Own is a long essay based on two lectures on women and fiction that Woolf read in 1928. Since then it became recognized as one of the most important feminist texts of the 20th century coining an acclaimed statement that "a woman must have money and a room of her own if she is to write fiction."

name: Tao Te Ching
label: simple
description: The Tao Te Ching is a Chinese classic text written around 400 BC and traditionally credited to the sage Laozi. Laozi was a semi-legendary ancient Chinese Taoist philosopher and his life is shrouded in many mysteries. But the Tao Te Ching is a fundamental text for both philosophical and religious Taoism. It also strongly influenced other schools of Chinese philosophy and religion. Many artists, including poets, painters, calligraphers, and gardeners, have used the Tao Te Ching as a source of inspiration. Its influence has spread widely within the globe’s artistic and academic spheres. Tao Te Ching is one of the most translated texts in world literature, it has been translated into Western languages over 250 times, mostly to English, German, and French. The first English translation of the Tao Te Ching was produced in 1868 by the Scottish Protestant missionary John Chalmers, entitled The Speculations on Metaphysics, Polity, and Morality of the "Old Philosopher" Lau-tsze. This one is the translation by James Legge. He produced it for Oxford’s Sacred Books of the East.

name: Dracula's Guest
label: simple
description: "Dracula’s Guest" is a collection of nine short stories by Bram Stoker, published posthumously in 1914 by his widow, Florence Balcombe. This collection highlights Bram Stoker’s versatility beyond "Dracula", offering a range of supernatural and gothic tales that explore themes of fear, guilt, revenge, and the supernatural. "Dracula’s Guest", in particular, provides additional context and depth to the lore of "Dracula", making it a valuable piece for enthusiasts of Stoker’s work. Stoker’s stories are characterized by their atmospheric settings, intricate plots, and exploration of the darker aspects of human nature. His use of suspense and detailed descriptions creates a palpable sense of dread, drawing readers into his macabre world. The collection not only entertains but also reflects the Victorian fascination with the supernatural and the unknown.

name: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
label: simple
description: Washington Irving (1783-1859) was an American short-story writer, essayist, biographer, historian, and diplomat of the early 19th century. He is often called the "Father of American Literature". With skillful storytelling, Irving combines elements of suspense, humor, and folklore, creating an enduring tales that have captured the imagination of readers for generations.  The present collection features such famous short stories as The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, Rip Van Winkle, The Spectre Bridegroom and The Adventure of The Mysterious Picture.

name: A Holy Terror
label: simple
description: Ambrose Bierce (1842-1914) was an American short story writer, journalist, poet, and American Civil War veteran. A prolific and versatile writer, Bierce was regarded as one of the most influential journalists in the United States. His short stories rank alongside the works of Edgar Allan Poe and H.F. Lovecraft.  The present collection features such famous short stories as A Holy Terror, An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge, A Physiological Shipwreck, A Vine on a House and others.

name: The Beast in the Jungle | The Figure in the Carpet
label: simple
tags: The Beast in the Jungle | The Figure in the Carpet
description: Henry James (1843-1916) was an American- British writer and literary critic. 'The Beast in the Jungle' period of his work was marked with the use of exquisite narrative style, consisting in long winding sentences imitating the flow of spoken language, yet pursuing a single purpose and moving according to the chosen motif.  The book includes two short stories: 'The Beast in the Jungle' and 'The Figure in the Carpet.' Both of them feature characters obsessed with an idea. One is waiting for a horrible catastrophe to tramp on his life, and the other is desperate to reveal the secret, hidden between the lines of several novels and in the thoughts of his friends.

name: The Canterville Ghost
label: simple
description: Oscar Wilde, renowned for his wit, satire, and flamboyant personality, was a prolific Irish playwright, novelist, and poet of the late 19th century. "The Canterville Ghost," one of his lesser- known works, was first published in 1887 as a short story. This piece diverges from Wilde's usual style of social satire and instead presents a delightful blend of humor, parody, and supernatural elements. Despite its comedic tone, "The Canterville Ghost" also contains moments of poignancy, particularly in Sir Simon's backstory and his eventual redemption.

name: On the Pleasure of Hating
label: simple
description: William Hazlitt (1778-1830) had many talents. He was a painter, a writer, a journalist, a literary critic and a philosopher of sort. His essays have formed a thought-provoking collection of observations on human nature. The themes of the essays in this book touch on different subjects from the philosophical contemplations to the political observations. They all have in common one thing the insightful eloquence of William Hazlitt.

name: The Dead
label: simple
description: This book contains several short stories by James Joyce, published in 1914. Set in early 20th century Dublin, each story offers a glimpse into the lives of ordinary Dubliners, capturing moments of epiphany, disillusionment, and stagnation. Joyce's meticulous attention to detail and his use of symbolism illuminate the social, political, and psychological realities of Dublin at the time. "The Dead" is one of the most iconic stories written by Joyce: simple, yet lyric and profound.

name: Bartleby, The Scrivener
label: simple
description: Herman Melville (1819-1891) was an American writer. He is quite famous nowadays and is acknowledged to be one of the classics. In his days, however, the situation wasn't so bright for him. His first books were a huge success, but later works were considered too strange. He was forgotten afterwards until the readers rediscovered him in the XX century.  "The Bartleby" tells a story of a scrivener hired to copy documents for an attorney on Wall Street. Exposed to everyday grind he suddenly changes and chooses to stare at the wall instead, a decision that resonates well with modern readers.

name: Shooting an Elephant
label: simple
description: George Orwell was a man of many contradictions. He was a police officer in Burma, acting as instrument of the colonial politics. He abandoned this profession later to become a dishwasher in Paris and London, facing himself the hardships of the poor and the working class. This experience formed Orwell as a democratic socialist, and his political beliefs were a significant part of his identity. His writing is clear and concise and still resonates with a reader today.

name: The Gold-Bug
label: simple
description: Edgar Allan Poe (1809-1849) was an American writer, poet and literary critic. He was praised for the minuteness of detail, analytical subtlety and refined language. The power he had over the reader was so astonishing that, despite accusations of immorality and abundance of gore, Poe's short stories were widely acclaimed and warmly accepted by both critics and readers.  The present collection features such famous short stories as The Gold-Bug, The Murders in the Rue Morgue, The Fall of the House of Usher, and William Wilson.

name: Death in the Woods
label: simple
description: Sherwood Anderson (1876-1941) was an American writer, whose works greatly influenced Ernest Hemingway and William Faulkner. His short stories revive the traditions of oral narration by introducing an extremely fragile and credible narrator, honest to a fault - and yet conscious of his audience and seeking to make an impression. He depicts the transitional moments in characters' lives moments of awakening and truth, buried under the layers of mundane immovability and sloth.

name: Love of Life
label: simple
description: Jack London (1876-1916) was an American journalist and writer. He went through the Klondike Gold Rush, saw the Russo-Japanese War and supported the socialist movement in the United States. He adopted his life experience for the breathtaking short stories and novels that tell tales of the Northern frosty wilderness and struggles of men - and became the first American writer to earn a substantial amount of money through his works. The collection includes London's three short stories: "Love of Life", a hymn to human perseverance and strength, "To Build a Fire", a story of arrogance in the face of extreme cold, and "The Mexican", an account of a fight, where losing a battle means losing the revolution.

name: The Monkey's Paw
label: simple
description: W. W. Jacobs (1863-1943) was an English writer primarily known through his short stories. From the iconic 'The Monkey's Paw' to lesser-known gems, Jacobs delved into the darker corners of human nature, exploring themes of fate, greed, and the supernatural. With masterful storytelling and a keen eye for suspense, Jacobs weaved tales that linger in the mind long after the final page is turned. Jacobs masterfully crafted an atmosphere of suspense and dread, leaving readers captivated by the eerie twists and cautionary lessons embedded within each tale.

name: The Gift of the Magi
label: simple
description: O. Henry (William Sydney Porter; 1862-1910) was an American writer best known for his short stories. He found his characters on the streets while talking to laborers, tramps, clerks - he listened to everyone he met or passed. One key element of his short stories was surprise an extraordinary plot twist, an improbable ending, the turn of events not unlike ones in fairy tales. Readers adored O. Henry’s writing not only for the magic it contained, but also for his attention to the least remarkable and for the sympathy and warmth with which he wrote about them. The collection includes twelve of the most famous short stories by O. Henry.

name: Death on the Nile | Смерть на Ниле
label: simple
tags: Death on the Nile | Смерть на Ниле

name: The secret garden
label: simple
description: Mary Lennox is an unwanted child. Spoilt, bad-tempered and orphaned, she has to go to her uncle of whom she knows nothing. Her uncle, lost in his own miseries, doesn’t want to know much about her either. Mary lives now in a big gloomy house that has a hundred rooms and its secrets are even more. Somebody cries there at night. The only escape from the house are the gardens enclosing it. Walking there, fighting with a wind, Mary starts to change. She becomes stronger and learns what it is – to be happy. But there are mysteries to unravel still. Near the house, there is a secret garden hidden behind the walls. It is connected with some tragedy, mysterious like everything in the estate and probably very beautiful. Mary starts her search of this secret garden; the search that will transform her and all the people around her.

name: Pygmalion
label: simple
description: Bernard Shaw never aimed to please-he aimed to provoke, to unsettle, and, ideally, to make you laugh at your own absurdities. His plays aren’t comfortable amusements; they’re sharp, deliberate jabs at the hypocrisies we like to pretend don’t exist. In Pygmalion, Shaw gives us Eliza Doolittle, a flower girl transformed into a duchess in speech and manner, only to find herself adrift-an experiment perfected but no longer needed. In Mrs. Warren’s Profession, a daughter proud of her independence discovers it was bought by her mother’s "undignified" choices and has to face the fact that not only the society consists of double-faced pricks but that she is herself one of them.

name: The war of the worlds
label: simple
description: What if we are not alone in this cold black universe? What if there are other sentient beings among stars? Would that be a relief? I’m afraid not. H.G. Wells’ The War of the Worlds tells the story of a sudden and devastating Martian invasion of Earth. The aliens arrive in massive cylinders, bringing advanced technology and deadly weapons. Humanity is powerless against their destructive heat - rays and poisonous gases. As the Martians wreak havoc, the story shows mankind’s place in the universe, reminding us of the fragility of life.

name: The Hamlet
label: simple
description: The first novel of Faulkner’s Snopes trilogy, The Hamlet is both an ironic take on classical tragedy and a mordant commentary on the grand pretensions of the antebellum South and the depths of its decay in the aftermath of the war and Reconstruction. It tells of the advent and rise of the Snopes family in Frenchman’s Bend, a small town built on the ruins of a once-stately plantation. Flem Snopes - wiley, energetic, a man of shady origins - quickly comes to dominate the town and its people with his cunning and guile.

name: The wild palms
label: simple
description: In this feverishly beautiful novel-originally titled If I Forget Thee, Jerusalem-William Faulkner interweaves two narratives, each wholly absorbing in its own right, each subtly illuminating the other. In New Orleans in 1937, a man and a woman embark on a headlong flight into the wilderness of illicit passion, fleeing her husband and the temptations of respect- ability. In Mississippi ten years earlier, a convict sets forth across a flooded river, risking his one chance at freedom to rescue a pregnant woman. From these separate stories, Faulkner composes a symphony of deliverances and damnation, survival and self-sacrifice.

name: The reivers
label: simple
description: In this comic masterpiece, eleven-year-old Lucius Priest is persuaded by Boon Hogganbeck, a family retainer, to steal his grandfather's car and make a trip to Memphis. The Priests' black coachman, Ned McCaslin, stows away, and the three of them embark on a heroic odyssey for which none of them is prepared. They wind up at Miss Reba's Memphis bordello, and from there wild misadventures ensue- involving horse smuggling, trainmen, sheriff's deputies, and jail

name: The unvanquished
label: simple
description: The Unvanquished features the Sartoris family, who embody the ideal of Southern honor and its transformation through war, defeat, and Reconstruction: Colonel John Sartoris, who is murdered by a business rival after the war; his son, Bayard, who learns a new kind of courage by refusing to kill; Cousin Drusilla, a young war widow who rides with Sartoris's cavalry; and Granny Rosa Millard, the matriarch, who must put aside her code of gentility to survive.

name: Intruder in the dust
label: simple
description: At once an engrossing murder mystery and an unflinching portrait of racial injustice, Intruder in the Dust is the story of Lucas Beauchamp, a black man wrongly arrested for the murder of a white man, Vinson Gowrie. Confronting the threat of lynching, Lucas sets out to prove his innocence, aided by a white lawyer, Gavin Stevens, and his young nephew, Chick Mallison.

name: Passive income, Aggressive retirement
label: simple
genres: Shaxsiy rivojlanish uchun adabiyotlar; Iqtisodiyot va Moliyaga oid adabiyotlar
description: Two million dollars. That’s how much money someone under age 40 will need to accumulate to retire. That often means working 40-hour weeks and penny - pinching your whole life. How else could you save a cool $2 mil? Finance guru, former financial advisor, and Amazon bestselling author of Money Honey, Rachel Richards has one goal in mind: teaching you everything you need to know to become financially free earlier than you ever thought possible. At age 27, Rachel quit her job and retired, living off $10,000+ per month in passive income streams. Let her show you how to do it at any age - it’s never too late.

name: The obstacle is the way
label: simple
description: We are stuck, stymied, frustrated. But it needn’t be this way. There is a formula for success that’s been followed by the icons of history - from John D. Rockefeller to Amelia Earhart to Ulysses S. Grant to Steve Jobs - a formula that showed them how to turn obstacles into opportunities. Faced with impossible situations, they produced the astounding triumphs we all seek. These men and women were not exception- ally brilliant, lucky, or gifted. Their success came from timeless philosophical principles laid down by a Roman emperor who struggled to articulate a method for excellence in any and all situations. This book reveals that formula in a new way - and shows us how we can turn our own adversity into advantage.

name: What everybody is saying
label: simple
description: Read this book and send your nonverbal intelligence soaring. Joe Navarro, a former FBI counterintelligence officer and a recognized expert on nonverbal behavior, explains how to "speed-read" people: decode sentiments and behaviors, avoid hidden pitfalls, and look for deceptive behaviors. You’ll also learn how your body language can influence what your boss, family, friends, and strangers think of you.

name: The rules of people
label: simple
description: These Rules are the guiding principles that show you how to connect with anyone, build strong relationships with friends and colleagues, and even get the best out of difficult people. They will help you say the right thing, do the right thing, and know instinctively how to handle every situation.

name: The rules of life
label: simple
description: The Rules of Life are the guiding principles that will help you get more out of life, shrug off adversity more easily and generally be a happier, calmer, more fulfilled person. You'll feel the benefits, and so will everyone around you.

name: The rules of work
label: simple
description: For some people, work is a breeze. They glide effortlessly onwards and upwards, always saying and doing the right thing, getting paid more, getting promotions, getting results.  Is there something successful people know that we don’t? You bet there is. They know the Rules of work.  These Rules are the guiding principles that will improve what you do and how you do it. They will give you the unmistakable air of confidence that will win you admiration, respect, and help you towards your next promotion. In this new edition of the international bestseller, Richard Templar has added 10 new Rules to help you get heard, noticed, acknowledged and followed.  To get ahead and stay on top, you need The Rules of Work.

name: The good girl's guide to being a d*ck
label: simple
tags: The good girl's guide to being a d*ck
description: This book will teach you how to embrace your inner badass, guide you through who and what to get rid of from your life, help you stop worrying about what others think, and show you how the seemingly small things in life can have a huge impact on the quality of your everyday living. You’ll learn to embrace your own needs and desires, and in doing so, become more passionate about the things you love. You can live the life you’ve always wanted - free of guilt or baggage.

name: The Sea - Wolf
label: simple
genres: Badiiy adabiyotlar; Jahon adabiyoti; Sarguzasht; Psixologiya
description: "The Sea-Wolf," a psychological adventure novel, plunges readers into the tumultuous life of Humphrey van Weyden, an erudite literary critic whose fate takes a dramatic turn. Plucked from the jaws of death following a catastrophic ferry accident, van Weyden finds himself aboard the "Ghost", a sealing schooner helmed by the formidable Wolf Larsen. What begins as a passive observation of his new surroundings swiftly transforms into a fierce battle for survival as van Weyden grapples with the relentless brutality of the sea and Larsen’s merciless creed of social Darwinism. "The Sea-Wolf" published in 1904 is a significant work in Jack London’s work, illustrating his ability to blend adventure with deep philosophical inquiry. It offers a critique of contemporary society and explores the fundamental aspects of human nature and survival. Through harrowing trials and existential confrontations, "The Sea-Wolf" dissects power dynamics, moral ambiguity, and the resilience of the human spirit. Over a century later, it remains a riveting narrative, as compelling and thought-provoking as the day it was penned.

name: To the lighthouse
label: simple
description: «To the Lighthouse» by Virginia Woolf is a modernist novel exploring themes of time, reality, and gender roles. It follows the Ramsay family and their guests over a decade, using a stream-of-consciousness narrative to delve into their inner lives. The novel is structured in three parts: «The Window,» capturing a single day; «Time Passes», depicting the passage of ten years; and «The Lighthouse,» concluding with a long-anticipated journey. Woolf critiques societal norms and highlights the fluidity of reality and the struggles for artistic and personal independence.

name: A portrait of the artist as a young man
label: simple
tags: A portrait of the artist as a young man
description: "A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man" by James Joyce is a novel that delves into the inner world of its protagonist, Stephen Dedalus, as he navigates the complexities of religion, nationality, and artistic expression in early 20th-century Ireland. Throughout the novel, Joyce employs stream-of-consciousness narrative techniques, intricate symbolism, and rich language to explore Stephen’s inner turmoil and quest for self-realization. The title itself suggests the novel’s focus on the development of an artist’s identity amid the constraints of society and tradition.

name: The Jungle Book
label: simple
description: In the heart of the lush and untamed Indian jungle, a young boy named Mowgli embarks on a thrilling journey in “The Jungle Book”. This classic tale, penned by Rudyard Kipling, has captivated audiences of all ages for generations. Abandoned as a baby and raised by a pack of wolves, Mowgli grows up learning the laws of the jungle from his wise mentor, the black panther Bagheera, and the affable bear Baloo. As he navigates through the exotic and perilous wilderness, he meets a myriad of fascinating creatures, from the cunning python Kaa to the formidable tiger Shere Khan. As he matures and gains wisdom, Mowgli becomes torn between two worlds: the wild, free-spirited jungle he calls home and the world of men that beckons him with its allure. In this struggle, he must confront his own identity and find a place where he truly belongs.

name: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
label: simple
description: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist, essayist, poet and travel writer. Despite the fact that his grandfather and father were engineers, Robert decided to pursue his life to writing. "Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde" is a famous Gothic novel, which portrays the enthralling battle between two contrasting personalities, one representing inherent goodness and the other embodying pure evil. Set in Victorian London, the story delves into the depths of the human soul, embarking on a terrifying and chilling journey. Through the eyes of Mr. Utterson, a lawyer and friend of Dr. Jekyll, the narrative unfolds, exploring the distressing struggle between good and evil. As the suspense builds, Mr. Utterson becomes determined to uncover the truth behind the mysterious connection between Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.

name: The time machine
label: simple
description: H. G. Wells was a pioneer of science fiction. He was a sort of time machine himself, his mind moving across the vast distances of space, making stories about the imagined future or the long-forgotten past. "The Time Machine" is one of the first books on time- traveling. The main protagonist builds a time machine and goes to the distant future. There he finds that humanity still still lives on Earth, but evolution pulled a bizarre joke on it...

name: Tales of horror
label: simple
description: "Tales of Horror" plunges readers into Edgar Allan Poe’s labyrinth of fear, where madness whispers through the walls and the unknown lurks in every shadow. This collection of his most unsettling stories reveals a world where guilt takes on a pulse of its own, vengeance is served with chilling precision, and the line between life and death dissolves into nightmare. From the feverish paranoia of "The Tell-Tale Heart" to the suffocating dread of "The Cask of Amontillado" and the decaying grandeur of "The Fall of the House of Usher", Poe weaves tales that burrow deep into the psyche, leaving behind an eerie unease that lingers long after the last page. More than mere ghost stories, these narratives explore the fragile nature of sanity, the weight of buried secrets, and the monstrous depths of human obsession. "Tales of Horror" is an invitation into the beautifully grotesque imagination of a writer whose words still echo in the dark corners of literature.

name: The war of the worlds
label: simple
description: What if we are not alone in this cold black universe? What if there are other sentient beings among stars? Would that be a relief? I’m afraid not. H.G. Humanity is powerless against their destructive heat - rays and poisonous gases. As the Martians wreak havoc, the story shows mankind’s place in the universe, reminding us of the fragility of life.

name: Agnes Grey
label: simple
description: After her family falls into poverty due to a disastrous financial venture, Agnes Grey resolves to work as a governess to supplement their scant income and claim her independence. Resolute and clear-eyed, she ventures into the world, only to face the tumultuous challenges of managing unruly children and confronting the haughty indifference of their parents. Her solace comes in the form of Mr. Weston, a curate who offers kindness in a world where it is scarce.

name: The ransom of red chief and other stories
label: simple
tags: The ransom of red chief and other stories
description: O. Henry, the pen name of William Sydney Porter, was a masterful American writer known for his mastery of the short story format. The collection of stories encompasses an anthology of his most renowned works, showcasing the author’s unique style and storytelling ability. "The Ransom of Red Chief" tells the story of two swindlers in need of money. To earn it, Bill and Sam decide to do something terrible: they want to kidnap the son of one of the townspeople and demand a ransom for him. They succeed, of course; however, they soon find themselves at the mercy of the mischievous and unruly child who turns the tables on them.

label: simple
description: "The Call of the Wild" is a collection of short stories by Jack London, immersing the reader in the world of harsh nature and the struggle for survival. In these stories, the characters face extreme challenges, showing courage and perseverance. London masterfully describes primitive instincts and dramatic conflicts between man and the environment, creating exciting and intense plots.

name: Surrounded by setbacks
label: simple
description: Ever feel like throwing in the towel? Whatever you’re facing - be it redundancy, a relationship catastrophe or yet another job rejection – when life goes off-track, you need the right strategy! Drawing on the simple four-colour behavioural model made famous in the internationally bestselling Surrounded by Idiots, this entertaining read is here to give you the tools to take back control and pave the way to a brighter future. At some point we will all face the unexpected, but with Thomas Erikson’s unique method, you can turn any setback into success.

name: Surrounded by vampires
label: simple
description: Do you often feel exhausted by conversations? Are there people in your life who belittle you through words or actions? Or, do you have colleagues who take up all your time? You could be surrounded by vampires! Be it time, energy, attention or habit vampires, these ubiquitous social villains can leave you feeling drained and depleted. Whether they’re lurking in your office, hiding amongst friends and family, or invading your thoughts, vampires can be found all around you. Fortunately, no vampire can survive when the sun shines on them. With the help of the behavioural model made famous in Surrounded by Idiots, international bestselling author and behavioural expert Thomas Erikson will help you recognise and banish the vampires in your life.

name: How will you measure your life?
label: simple
tags: How will you measure your life?
description: This book doesn’t offer easy answers. Instead, it will prompt you to consider the most important questions you’ll ever face. It won’t tell you what to think. Instead, it aims to teach you how to think about your life and your purpose by sharing powerful research and theories about success and failure that were developed at Harvard Business School and other institutions. It won’t prescribe a set path to happiness. Instead, it will equip you to lead the type of life to which you truly aspire. Contained within this book are the same tools that have allowed managers to lead companies that have gone on to change the world. Think of it as a guidebook for your future. The theories and situations summarized here will help you understand the critical decisions that can bring happiness and success in life instead of sadness and disappointment.

name: The 5 love languages
label: simple
description: BETWEEN BUSY SCHEDULES AND LONG DAYS, expressing love can fall by the wayside. We forget to compliment, to give gifts "just because," to linger in our embrace. The things that say "I love you" seem to either not get said or not get through. This is a book about saying it and hearing it clearly. No gimmicks. No psychoanalyzing. Just learning to express love in your spouse’s language. WITH OVER 20 MILLION COPIES SOLD, The 5 Love Languages" has transformed countless relationships. Its ideas are simple and conveyed with clarity and humor, making this book as practical as it is personable. You’ll be inspired by real-life stories and encouraged by its commonsense approach. Reading this book feels like taking a walk with a wise friend. Applying it will forever change your relationship -starting today.

name: Kiss that frog!
label: simple
description: Just like the lonely princess in the fairy tale who was reluctant to lock lips with a warty frog and transform him into a handsome prince, something stops many of us short of attaining our dreams. Our negative thoughts, emotions, and attitudes can threaten to keep us from achieving all that we’re capable of. In Kiss That Frog! bestselling author and speaker Brian Tracy and his daughter, therapist Christina Tracy Stein, provide a set of practical, proven strategies anyone can use to turn those negative frogs into positive princes. Tracy and Stein present a step-by-step plan that addresses the root causes of negativity, helps you uncover blocks that have become mental obstacles, and shows how you can transform them into stepping-stones to achieve your fullest potential.

name: The Charisma Myth
label: simple
description: What if charisma could be taught? The charisma myth is the idea that charisma is a fundamental, inborn quality you either have it (Bill Clinton, Steve Jobs, Oprah) or you don’t. But that’s simply not true, as Olivia Fox Cabane reveals. Charismatic behaviors can be learned and perfected by anyone. Drawing on techniques she originally developed for Harvard and MIT, Cabane breaks down charisma into its components. Becoming more charismatic doesn’t mean transforming your fundamental personality. It’s about adopting a series of specific practices that fit in with the personality you already have.

name: Change your world
label: simple
description: Problems surround us: division, anger, violence, corruption, poverty, homelessness, and family breakdown. Too often, we feel powerless to do anything about them. We wonder, Why doesn’t somebody do something? The good news is, somebody can. YOU can be the one who changes the world around you. John C. Maxwell and Rob Hoskins have spent their lives as catalysts for change. They started small, simply helping others where they were because they wanted to add value to people. Over decades of making a difference, they developed a straightforward blueprint for creating positive change. Now they want to share their stories of change and teach you how to make a difference. Whether you are leading a large organization, running a small business, going to school, volunteering your time, or raising a family, Maxwell and Hoskins will show you how to change your world for the better. You can be the change you want to see in the world.
